content.title: About
content.content: Cream of Wheat is a finely milled wheat semolina that cooks into a smooth, creamy porridge. It is commonly served for breakfast with milk, cream, fruit, or honey.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial version appeared in the United States in the early 20th century under the Cream of Wheat brand.
The product is made from the endosperm of wheat, so it is gluten‑free only when produced from gluten‑free wheat varieties.
Its soft texture makes it a popular choice for infant and toddler nutrition.
In the 1930s the company introduced flavored varieties such as vanilla and cinnamon.
The cereal is a good source of iron, which is why it has been marketed for people with anemia.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Cream of Wheat provides easily absorbable iron that supports normal blood formation.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains thiamine, niacin and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The fine semolina cooks quickly and is gentle on the stomach, making it suitable for children and sensitive adults.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The product contains virtually no fat, which fits well into low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Small amounts of calcium and magnesium contribute to bone strength.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Traditional Cream of Wheat contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: It can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should consume it with caution.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to wheat, experiencing skin or gastrointestinal reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Prepare by whisking the dry semolina into hot milk or water and cooking for 2–3 minutes until thickened. Add butter, honey, fresh berries, dried fruit, or nuts for flavor and extra nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed container. After opening, use within 3–4 weeks, or keep refrigerated for longer storage to prevent moisture and mold.

ham-and-rice-with-mushroom-sauce.title: Ham and rice with mushroom sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Ham and rice with mushroom sauce is a ready‑to‑eat dish consisting of boiled rice, tender pieces of ham, and a creamy mushroom sauce made from mushrooms, cream, and seasonings. It is popular in cafeterias and as a quick home meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mushroom sauce gives the dish a rich umami flavor and silky texture.
Ham is usually made from pork loin that is smoked or boiled, resulting in a tender product.
Long‑grain rice is often used to keep the grains separate and fluffy.
The dish reheats well in a microwave while retaining its taste.
Combining protein (ham) and carbohydrates (rice) makes it a balanced source of energy.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Rice delivers quick‑acting carbohydrates that fuel active lifestyles.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both ham and mushrooms are rich in B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish contains iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Mushrooms add a modest amount of fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Ham often contains a lot of salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Nitrites and preservatives
items.content: Some hams may contain nitrites, which are undesirable in excess.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to mushrooms.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The cream‑based sauce makes the dish relatively calorie‑rich; adjust portions if dieting.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, optionally garnished with fresh herbs such as parsley or dill. It works as a standalone meal or as part of a larger menu with a side salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it retains quality for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

spaghetti-sauce-with-seafood-and-added-v.title: Spaghetti sauce with seafood and added vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Spaghetti sauce with seafood and added vegetables is a ready‑to‑use tomato‑based sauce enriched with pieces of shrimp, mussels, squid and a mix of vegetables (carrot, celery, onion, bell pepper). It is designed for quick pasta meals, combining the briny taste of the sea with the freshness of vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sauce often contains olive oil and aromatic herbs such as basil and oregano.
Seafood is lightly sautéed before being mixed in, preserving its tenderness and flavor.
Vegetables are diced finely, boosting the nutritional value of the product.
The sauce can be used not only with spaghetti but also with other pasta shapes, rice dishes, or as a base for casseroles.
Thanks to heat processing, the product has a long shelf life without the need for artificial preservatives.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood such as shrimp and mussels provides omega‑3s that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of high‑quality protein
items.content: Shrimp, mussels and squid deliver complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The added vegetables contribute vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium and folate, supporting immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using olive oil instead of butter keeps saturated fat levels moderate.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Tomatoes and vegetables are high in dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: People with shellfish allergies may experience reactions ranging from mild to anaphylactic after consuming the sauce.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces can be high in salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Heat‑treatment of seafood
items.content: Improper reheating may leave seafood undercooked, increasing the risk of foodborne illness.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Tomato sauces are often sweetened; those watching blood sugar should be aware of the amount.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the sauce in a saucepan or microwave, add cooked spaghetti and stir. Optionally garnish with fresh herbs, grated Parmesan, or a drizzle of olive oil for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep it refrigerated and use within 5 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.

taco-flour-tortilla-pork-with-beans-chee.title: Flour Tortilla Taco with Pork, Beans and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A flour tortilla taco filled with pork, beans and cheese is a classic Mexican fast‑food item. The soft wheat tortilla is lightly toasted, while the interior combines juicy pork, seasoned beans and melted cheese for a balanced flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat flour tortillas originated in northern Mexico in the 19th century as an alternative to corn tortillas.
Traditional fillings include marinated pork (al pastor) and black beans, but modern versions use a variety of cheeses.
Tacos are designed to be eaten by hand, making them a popular street‑food staple.
The combination of protein (pork, cheese) and beans provides a complete amino‑acid profile.
In the United States, Taco Bell popularized the “soft” tortilla version rather than the crispy shell.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pork and cheese are good sources of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Beans supply soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and blood‑sugar stability.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Both pork and beans contribute dietary iron, important for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pork is rich in vitamin B12, while beans provide folate, together supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, which is vital for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Pork and cheese can contain saturated fats; individuals monitoring cholesterol should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Cheese and marinades often add significant sodium, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat tortillas contain gluten and are unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Warm the tortilla on a skillet or grill, then add hot pork, drained beans and shredded cheese. Fold into a triangle or roll and serve with salsa, guacamole or sour cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared tacos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Store pork and beans separately in the fridge for no more than 2 days. For freezing, wrap each tortilla tightly in plastic film and store up to 2 months.
